shipped_rows.title_o: Increased conspiracy beliefs among ethnic and Muslim minorities

blind_target.title: Why education predicts decreased belief in conspiracy theories
blind_target.evidence_quote: The main aim of the study was to replicate and extend van Prooijen's findings on how education and its outcomes (cognitive complexity, subjective social standing, self‐esteem, a feeling of control and powerlessness, cognitive reflection, epistemic curiosity and scientific reasoning) predict conspiracy beliefs.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract identifies the target and reports the present mediators and negative education association, but does not state which original mediator findings were confirmed or contradicted or supply an overall replication verdict. A shared education association alone cannot settle the replication of the multiple targeted pathways.

luna_triage.reason: Abstract explicitly says the two-study paper aims to replicate and extend van Prooijen’s findings; bibliography identifies the 2017 target. The sole shipped original (2018, ethnic and Muslim minorities) is a separate paper and does not represent it. Abstract-only evidence limits finer characterization of which pathways were retested, but direct replication and identity are explicit.
